Sir, I rise here to oppose the Motion of Thanks moved by Dr. Mahesh 
Chandra Sharma, on the President's Address to both Houses of 
Parliament. I have got high regard for our hon. President; Shri K.R. 
Narayanan. But, at the risk of being repetitive, I would say that when I 
heard the speech which was read for over an hour, time and again, it 
appeared to me that it was a compendium of Annual Reports of 
different Departments of the Governme nt of India. However, Sir, I can 
speak only on that. I cannot create another speech. In paragraph 4, 
the President says, "What happened on December 13 was the nadir of 
a long list of reprehensible acts in  a twenty-year long campaign of 
cross-border terrorism against India." Sir, it is quite amusing to note 
that the Government of this country  is talking of 20 years of campaign 
against cross-border terrorism. I would like to know' since when they 
realised that cross-border terrorism is a major problem for this country. 
Did they realise it since 1998? When Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee went to 
Lahore with much fanfare and signed the Lahore Declaration, along 
with Shri Nawaz Sharif, the deposed Prime Minister of Pakistan, not a 
single sentence was inscribed on cross-border terrorism. So, cross-
border terrorism is a terminology which the Government of India, this 
present Government, evolved after the Kargil conflict. So, how do you 
say that it is a 20-year long camp aign against cross-border terrorism, 
etc., etc.? Moreover, how did this cross-border terrorism garner so 
much of strength? The Government of  India is refusing to understand, 
even though it has been pointed out time and again in this House by 
different Members, that the terro rism which is being sponsored, 
pioneered, nurtured, developed, in some of the countries, has its allies 
in this country. They find soft recrui ts, because there is a plenty of 
abject poverty here; there is unemplo yment; there is problem of social 
alienation. The vast number of unemployed and socially alienated 
people, who have been discriminated against by the policies of the 
successive Governments, have become a soft target for these 
terrorists, for the sponsors of cross-border terrorism. Unless the 
Government of India takes some def inite measures to address this 
perennial problem of abject poverty and social alienation, you can't 
simply take care of the problem of cross-border terrorism. I have 
talked about this, time and again, *. in this House. 
It is not the question of only Jammu and Kashmir, but it is the 
question of entire India, and particul arly those States where the social 
alienation is more and social discrimination is more. It is more visible 
in the

parts of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, some parts of Maharashtra and

been unleashed from the bottle-the demon of fundamentalism, the

are deprived of any such opportuni ty. The Government admits that 
there are nearly four crores of  unemployed youth, both women and 
men. If we add the rural unemployment, the figure would be

STATEMENT BY MINISTER 
The incident at the Army Recruitment Rally at Lucknow on 14th 
March, 2002 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES): 
Mr. Vice-Chairman, Sir, a recruitment rally had been scheduled in 
Lucknow Cantonment Area from 13 th March, 2002 to 31 st March, 
2002. On 14th March, 2002, about 5,000 young men had assembled at 
the Cantonment 
305 

RAJYA SABHA [15 MARCH, 2002]  
Area for the recruitment rally. At approximately 0600 hours over 100 
of these young boys who had also come to participate in the 
recruitment rally, were sitting on the concrete roof of a sewage tank, 
waiting for the rally activities to begin. 
Probably due to the overload, the sewage tank roof collapsed 
and several young men fell into the tank. Prompt rescue and relief 
operations were launched to save the victims. 21 dead bodies have 
been recovered. Three injured young men are under treatment in 
Command hospital. 
The tragic incident triggered off mob violence by the large 
crowds which had gathered for the recruitment rally. Police 
reinforcements had to be rushed to the site to control the situation. A 
number of civil and army vehicles  have been damaged by the mob. 
The situation had been controlled by the police and the mob had been 
dispersed from the cantonment area by afternoon. The mob had also 
damaged some civil vehicles in the civil area adjoining the 
cantonment. 
Hon. Prime Minister has announced an ex-gratia relief of Rs.1 
lakh each to the families of those who have died in this tragic incident. 
In addition, the Government of Uttar Pradesh has also announced an 
ex-gratia relief of Rs.1  lakh each to the fa milies of those who have 
died, Rs.25,ooo each to those who are severely injured and Rs.5000 
each to those who have received minor injuries. 
A Court of Inquiry has been ordered by the Central Command 
into this unfortunate incident. 
As per the latest information received, the death toll of the 
tragic incident which occurred at the recruitment rally site in Lucknow 
Cantonment Area on 14 th March, 2002, has reached 23. 3 more 
casualties which had been taken out from the tank and taken away to 
some local civil hospital were later reported by the civil administration. 
2 persons out of these three causalities succumbed to injuries in the 
hospital; one person still remains in  the civil hospital and is under 
medical treatment. Therefore, the total death toll has come to 23.  
As per the information received the tragic incident had 
occurred at about 0555 hours on 14 th March, 2002. Within about 5 to 
10 minutes ambulances from Command and Base Hospitals had 
arrived on the scene of accident. One QRT Vehicle (Quick Recovery 
Transport) was also available on the rally site.     Because of the 
immediate assistance which became 
306 

[15 MARCH, 2002] RAJYA SABHA  
available the causalities from the tank were removed expeditiously 
and by about 0630 to 0640 hours, thes e casualties had been sent to 
the Command Hospital for treatment. 
His Excellency, the Governor of Uttar Pradesh had visited the 
site of incident around 1730 hours on I4 th March, 2002, and later also 
visited the Command Hospital and met the patients under treatment.
